solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sample spud stuffed with Stilton, primarily

indicators.note: a spud stuffed with something has it placed inside, so the next piece goes into the potato word

parts.note: tater is an informal word for a potato, as is spud

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of Stilton is used

explanation.surface: A baked potato filled with Stilton cheese offered as a little sample.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small portion given to try, which is what a sample is.

clue.text: Boring site with more rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash or knock about, so the letters of site and more are messed up

explanation.surface: A dull place with even more litter lying about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' looks like the litter, but it is the anagram signal on SITE + MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome is tedious and wearying, which is to say boring.

clue.text: Bug put in dry pot, finally

parts.note: to stick in is to put in or insert
sec is French for dry, used of wine

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of pot

explanation.surface: An insect placed into a dry pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' here means an insect, not a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick insect is a twig-like insect, and bug is a loose word for any insect.

clue.text: Bird in wren required to soar

indicators.note: to soar says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the bird is found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird is needed for a wren to fly high.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it signals the hidden run ENRE; 'to soar' turns it upward, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the sea eagle, a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Doggone clean?

parts.note: Spot is a classic name for a dog, so with the dog gone a thing is without its Spot: and something with no spots on it is perfectly clean

explanation.surface: An American exclamation of surprise at how clean something is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doggone' reads as the mild American oath, but split it as 'dog gone': Spot, the stock dog's name, is less.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with not a mark or blemish on it is immaculately clean.

clue.text: God: one dividing model and teacher

indicators.note: dividing says the one splits the other pieces apart by sitting between them

parts.note: to pose is to model, as for an artist
a don is a university teacher
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A deity who comes between a model and a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea.

clue.text: Substance added to meat reinserted when cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored or mixed up, like ingredients

explanation.surface: An ingredient put back into the meat as it cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderiser is a preparation applied to meat to soften its fibres.

clue.text: Farm animal in wood, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the word for the wood is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: yew is a tree and its wood

explanation.surface: A sheep in the woods, so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, kept on farms.

clue.text: Son tries to rough up sibling

indicators.note: to rough up is to knock about, so the letters of tries are mangled

explanation.surface: A boy tries to beat up his sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is a female sibling.

clue.text: Paradise not entirely equally divided up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the run is read from bottom to top
not entirely says only part of these words is used, a run lying inside them

explanation.surface: Paradise is not quite an equal share-out.
explanation.walkthrough: The run LLYDI sits inside 'equally divided', and 'up' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a blissful, perfect scene or time, a kind of paradise.

clue.text: In greed, revolutionary held power

indicators.note: something revolutionary overturns the existing order, so the letters of these words are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A greedy revolutionary seized and held power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like the person who held power, but it is the anagram signal working on IN GREED.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who reigned ruled as sovereign, that is held power.

clue.text: Dark lens used in Texas, for example?

indicators.note: in says the jumbled lens is placed inside the letters for Texas

parts.note: Texas is a state in the south of the US: S (south) and US

indicators.note: used here in the sense of worn and knocked about, so the letters of lens are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dark lens, the sort of sunglasses worn in sunny Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled LENS goes inside S + US. The question mark admits the irony: sunny Texas is hardly lacking sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A place without sunshine is dim and gloomy, so dark is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Good wine

definitions.meaning: as in 'for the ... of', meaning for the good or benefit of

explanation.definitionFit: Sake means benefit in 'for your sake', and is also the Japanese fermented rice drink.

clue.text: Unable to make a word, a little irate, not having a 'T' in Scrabble?

indicators.note: not having says the named letter is missing from the pool, so it is taken out before the rest are rearranged
to scrabble is to scramble or jumble, so the letters of a little irate are mixed up, with a nod to the word game

parts.note: a 'T' is a single letter T

explanation.surface: A Scrabble player, a little cross, is stuck without a T tile and cannot make a word.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle LITTLE IRATE and drop one T ('not having a T') to leave the ten letters. 'Scrabble' looks like the game but means scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone illiterate cannot read or write, so is unable to put a written word together.

clue.text: Potion I had with aspic or rum

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters of these words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A drink: I had something with aspic jelly, or perhaps rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink, but it is the old British word for odd, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphrodisiac is a love potion meant to arouse desire.

clue.text: A smashing place?

parts.note: smashing as in great, but also literally where glass is smashed: a recycling bin for empty bottles

explanation.walkthrough: A bottle bank is a British public container for recycling glass; bottles often break as they are dropped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass containers shatter in the recycling bin, so it is a site of breakage.

clue.text: Underling dressed '60s style?

parts.note: the miniskirt, or mini, was the signature fashion of the 1960s
dressed is ON, as in having clothes on

explanation.surface: A junior assistant turned out in swinging sixties fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'dressed '60s style' as 'with a mini on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion is a subordinate who does a superior's bidding, an underling.

clue.text: Snugly-fitting clothes on very soon

indicators.note: to clothe is to wrap or cover, so the word for snugly-fitting wraps around the next piece

parts.note: tight means fitting snugly, like close-fitting clothing

explanation.surface: Someone will be wearing their tight-fitting clothes very soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun for garments, but it is the verb meaning wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is later on this same day, so it arrives very soon.

clue.text: Emperor, European leader in office, relative claims

indicators.note: claims in the sense of takes hold of, so the relative's word wraps round the others

parts.note: nan is a grandmother, a relative
a Pole is a person from Poland, a European

indicators.note: leader in picks the first letter of office

explanation.surface: An emperor, a European leader in office, has a relative making claims.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French.

clue.text: Sea dog in strange American city

indicators.note: strange suggests something altered, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old sailor is out of place in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a port city in southern California.

clue.text: Treaty revised to protect a carrier

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so the jumbled letters enclose the a
a revised text has been reworked, so the letters of treaty are rearranged

explanation.surface: A treaty is amended to protect an aircraft carrier or similar vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: TEATRY, the anagram of TREATY, takes A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea tray is a flat board on which cups and pots are carried.

clue.text: High over an Italian city

indicators.note: high in the sense of intoxicated, so the letters of over an are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Flying high over an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' seems to describe altitude, but it is the anagram signal, meaning out of one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Verona is the city in northern Italy, setting of Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Confusing situation when other ranks brought into service

indicators.note: brought into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Mass is a church service
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are drafted into an occasion, causing confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the military term for enlisted soldiers below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is literally a bog, and figuratively a muddled, entangling mess.

clue.text: Possible provider of milk in the morning for tea

parts.note: an ass, a female donkey, can be milked
AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: Something to supply milk in the morning for one's tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk' and 'tea' suggest a cuppa, but the provider is a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a black tea grown in the northeast Indian state of that name.

clue.text: Where roof slates are free

definitions.meaning: slates sit ..., literally on top of the building
an idiom for given free by the establishment

explanation.definitionFit: Drinks on the house cost nothing, paid for by the bar; roof tiles physically sit on top of the building.

clue.text: Current turn

definitions.meaning: to turn, as a key or a crank

explanation.definitionFit: Moving air forms a stream like a current, and winding a clock means turning its key.

clue.text: Somewhat grateful, I feel, for time on this earth

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone feels rather thankful for their time on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A life is the span of existence a person has in this world.

clue.text: Dead calm

explanation.definitionFit: Gravestones say the deceased rests in peace, and a serene person is untroubled and tranquil.

clue.text: Short ball, ace

indicators.note: short says the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a prom is a formal dance, a ball

explanation.surface: A tennis player's short ball wins an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' and 'ace' suggest tennis, but the ball is a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro, a professional, is an expert, as is an ace.

clue.text: A misdeed with popular drug, stupid

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, a misdeed
in means fashionable or popular
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Committing a misdeed while on a fashionable drug is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine literally means donkey-like, and figuratively foolish or silly.

clue.text: Huge island capital transferring West Side to East

indicators.note: in an across answer west is the left; the left-hand side of the capital's name goes to the right-hand end

parts.note: Kingston is the capital of the island of Jamaica

explanation.surface: A huge island capital moves its West Side district over to the East.
explanation.walkthrough: KINGSTON splits into KING and STON; send KING from the left end to the right. STONKING is British slang for huge or tremendous.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonking is informal British slang for very large or impressive, so huge fits.

clue.text: Fastener left inside broken cover

indicators.note: inside says the L is placed within the rearranged letters
something broken is in pieces, so the letters of cover are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A fastener left inside a broken case or cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' makes VECRO from COVER, and 'inside' puts L into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Velcro is the hook-and-loop strip used to fasten clothing and bags.
